verdict.rationale: n8n's own docs include a built-in core node page titled "MCP Client" in its LangChain/AI node set, so it documents first-party support for connecting to external MCP servers. The evidence is only the page title, so how tools get exposed to agents, which transports are supported, and how authentication works are not shown. The MCP Server Trigger is the opposite role (n8n acting as a server) and is not credited here. Missing for 10: documented detail of connecting to external MCP servers and calling their tools from agents, transport/auth configuration, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can plug MCP servers into this product so it can use their tools
